points.description: States that a data member can be accessed from any member function of the class (class-wide scope). Equivalent wording such as 'available to all member functions' or 'usable throughout the class' earns the marks.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says data members belong to the class/object but does not clearly state that any member function can access them.

levels.says: Says data members are class-level or belong to the object, but does not state that all member functions can access them.

points.description: States that a local variable can only be accessed inside the member function that defines/declares it (function-local scope). Equivalent wording such as 'only usable in that function' or 'not visible to other functions' earns the marks.
points.partial_credit: Half marks if the answer says local variables are temporary or inside a function but does not clearly state that access is limited to that function.

levels.says: Says local variables are temporary or exist inside a function, but does not state that they cannot be accessed outside the defining function.

rubric.notes: Full marks require both sides of the contrast: data members are accessible from any member function of the class, and local variables only within the function that defines them. Award half of a point's marks when the answer gives only a vague version of that side without the access/scope limit. No marks for a side that is missing or wrong.
